direction_notes: Time-locked increases in RSU firing rate during tFUS, sensitive to PRF and duty cycle; FSU showed delayed-onset increases in firing rate rather than time-locked responses.

exposures.label: S1 tFUS, PRF and duty-cycle sweep

timing.protocol_description: Trials of 67 ms ultrasound duration were delivered every 2.5 s (10% jitter), 505 trials per parameter combination. PRF was swept (30, 300, 1500, 3000, 4500 Hz) at a fixed 200 microsecond tone-burst duration (TBD); PRF was then held at 1500 Hz while TBD was swept (40, 200, 400 microseconds), giving duty cycles of 6%, 30%, and 60%. A sham condition delivered the 1500 Hz PRF stimulus off-target toward the front of the skull.

source_quotes.n_subjects: 15 adult male Wistar rats were used in this study, each weighing approximately 250 g.
source_quotes.randomised: Parameters were recorded in a random order in each animal.
source_quotes.sham_type: We then implanted 5 more rats with chronic electrodes for head fixation, and at 7 months of age completed both awake and anesthetized recordings using 30 Hz and 1500 Hz PRF stimulation with 200 µs TBD, as well as a sham condition at 1500 Hz PRF with the ultrasound beam directed off target towards the front of the skull.
source_quotes.auditory_control: The sham condition allowed us to confirm that the activation we observed was not due to any auditory confound from off-target activation or skull conduction from the transducer.

flags.reason: ISPTA values across PRF conditions were calculated from a single measured peak-to-peak pressure via a pulse-intensity-integral formula, not independently measured for each PRF; the calculated value for 1500 Hz (30.13 mW/cm2) differs from the value the paper separately reports as directly measured for the same nominal condition (23.7071 mW/cm2, quoted under isppa_w_cm2).
Source text reads '300 H' where '300 Hz' is clearly intended (likely OCR/typesetting error); recorded as 300 Hz.

The paper states parameters were tested in random order within each animal (a within-subject design), not that subjects were randomised to groups; recorded as true but this may not map cleanly onto the randomised-groups sense of the field.
Sham used real ultrasound delivered off-target rather than a named auditory-masking method; classified as 'other' since it does not match a listed auditory_control category.

Recordings occurred across multiple ages/months (PRF tests, anesthesia tests, DC tests) with 2-3 recordings per head-fixation session, but paper does not state a single total number of sessions per subject.
